page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.3xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the x86_64 architecture and managed via a KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a dedicated 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor providing 6 physical cores and 12 vCPUs via hyperthreading. Cache architecture includes 32 KB L1 data cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 35 MB shared L3 cache, with instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, and AVX-512 VNNI. The instance is configured with 24.0 GB of system memory, matching a standard 1:2 compute-optimized ratio of 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps, while local storage is not provided, requiring external network-attached storage.

Benchmark results demonstrate mid-tier multithreaded capacity alongside modest single-core throughput. The instance recorded a Geekbench multi-core score of 5135.0, a PassMark CPU score of 10201.54, and a stress-ng multi-core result of 8856.27, all placing in the middle 50% tier. In contrast, single-threaded metrics reflect the lower baseline clock speed, with single-core Geekbench at 1018.0 and stress-ng at 1107.29, both falling into the bottom 25%. Memory bandwidth remains stable across larger transfers, recording 58.83 GB/sec uncached read and 49.38 GB/sec uncached write, though the overall PassMark memory score sits in the weak bottom 25% bracket.

Application-level performance aligns with general multi-threaded compute demands. Redis SET operations reached 8.65 million operations per second, while static web serving throughput achieved 8.31 GB/sec, reflecting average-tier throughput. Software compilation in Clang scored 8209.0, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression delivered 44.02 GB/sec. Large language model inference speeds reflect architecture constraints: while smaller 135M models achieve 656.59 prompt processing tokens per second, medium 7B models yield a weak 7.51 tokens per second during text generation due to the absence of dedicated GPU acceleration.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.c5.3xlarge delivers predictable dedicated compute resources suited for parallel batch processing, web application hosting, build systems, and microservices. Because it lacks bundled local NVMe storage and relies solely on remote storage attachments, workloads with extreme local disk IOPS requirements are constrained.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.c5.3xlarge is a compute-optimized x86_64 server instance featuring an Intel Xeon 8163 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It provides 12 dedicated vCPUs across 6 physical cores, supported by 24.0 GB of memory (2.0 GB per vCPU) and 4 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance includes no bundled local storage or dedicated hardware accelerators, necessitating external network block storage. Performance metrics position this instance in the middle tier for multi-core compute, delivering 8856.27 in stress-ng multi-core and 5135.0 in Geekbench multi-core, while single-thread speeds rank in the bottom quartile. Application benchmarks confirm steady throughput for Redis operations and static web serving. The instance is suited for multi-threaded batch jobs, web tier serving, and CI/CD compilation tasks.
